# CLean adaptation

These Lean sources come from Certora CLean at the
[pinned revision](https://github.com/Certora/clean/tree/123f7f7767e215aceb4821f0d044336d78103ade),
and `upstream.json` records the original file hashes. `LICENSE` is retained
from upstream; its list of dual-licensed files includes the `export/` directory
from which these sources originate. `LEAN.md` is the unchanged upstream
description of the whole `export/` directory, including the modules we leave
out and upstream's toolchain; it is not a report of local checks.

We keep `CCLib.lean` and the twenty modules of `CCLib/` that our proofs import:
the Clight and memory semantics (`AST`, `Archi`, `Clight`, `Cop`, `Ctypes`,
`Events`, `Floats`, `Globalenvs`, `Integers`, `Maps`, `Memdata`, `Memory`,
`Positive`, `Values`), the execution checker and its soundness proof
(`ClightExec`, `ClightExecSound`), the determinism of the step relation
(`Determinism`), and the lemmas on maps, memory data and memory that they use
(`MapsLemmas`, `MemdataLemmas`, `MemoryLemmas`). Nothing here imports upstream's
separation logic, Hoare logics, linking code and tactics (`Aggregate`, `FunPtr`,
`Funspec`, `Heap`, `Hoare`, `HoareArray`, `HoareLong`, `Linking`, `Locals`,
`SepHoare`, `SepLogic`, `Tactics`, `Temps`) or `Clightdefs.lean`, which only
gives files generated by `clightgen -lean` a module to import, so we do not
include them, and `CCLib.lean` imports only the modules we keep. In
`Determinism.lean`, two comments that named omitted modules now describe the
silent step relation directly. Our quadrature proofs use the execution rules
directly.

Local changes replace native floating-point arithmetic with FloatLib and
replace global external-call axioms with explicit environment parameters and
determinism contracts. Dependent semantic declarations carry those parameters.

Binary32 and binary64 operations use pure FloatLib definitions, including
arithmetic, comparisons, sign operations, and format conversions. Integer
conversion truncates the exact finite dyadic value and checks the destination
range; NaNs and infinities have no integer result. The four upstream external-call
axioms become an `ExternalCalls` environment and an
`ExternalCallsDeterministic` contract. Interpreter soundness holds for every
environment; determinism requires the contract.

The local port also uses the pinned Lean toolchain's names for conditional
simplification lemmas, and removes redundant tactics and a file-wide
unused-variable linter exception. The vendored `CCLib` target treats warnings
as errors. The `State.State` constructor retains its
upstream name for compatibility with exported programs; only that declaration
disables the duplicate-namespace linter. Upstream names, the layout of the
included modules, and licensing are unchanged.

The arithmetic follows FloatLib, including its NaN policy. This adaptation does
not prove agreement with Rocq's CompCert semantics, transfer the compiler
correctness theorem, or prove a particular quadrature program correct.

`scripts/check-lean.py` builds this library with the project and checks that its theorems,
private and generated ones included, use no axioms beyond `propext`, `Classical.choice` and
`Quot.sound`. The upstream example suite and differential tests are not part of this check.
